Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:86: After having spoken generally of the blemish in the covenant, and the punishment of one who emits seed in vain, we must explain another matter that also blemishes the covenant, which is the sin of nocturnal emission [keri] - for since it is an emission of seed in vain, it is a blemish in the covenant. And the explanation of KERI is that it "chills" [meikar, from the same root] that which is of the holy covenant from its place, bestowing it to the external force. And in the Zohar (Parashat Pekudei, page 264a), Chamber 2 of the Chambers of Impurity, which is the chamber in which retribution is exacted from whoever defiles his covenant - at the end of that chamber Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained that there are two spirits there that transform into males and females, and these make a person impure in a nighttime dream and cause him to emit seed in vain. And his punishment resembles somewhat the punishment for the sin of emitting seed in vain, for it is said (Deuteronomy 23:10), "and you shall guard yourself from every evil thing" - that he not have a forbidden thought by day and come to impurity at night (Avodah Zarah 20b) - and we have already copied above their teaching, of blessed memory (Niddah 13b), whoever brings himself to a state of forbidden thought is not admitted into the enclosure of the Holy One, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:87: And concerning the punishment of one who defiles himself, it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Metzora, page 55a) - these are its words: Rabbi Elazar said, it is written (Leviticus 15:31), "and you shall set apart the children of Israel from their impurity," and so on, "in defiling My tabernacle that is in their midst" - "and you shall set apart," like this "stranger" [zar], who is estranged from everyone, and does not attach himself to what is not his own. And come and see, at the time people become impure below, they become impure in everything, as we have stated - but at the time an impure spirit is aroused, do not think it is a stranger; rather, an impure spirit arouses another impure spirit, and it is given permission to descend to the world. What permission? The permission of holiness that would have descended and struck against it is no longer found, having departed - and then judgment is revealed against the guilty ones, and judgment is added upon judgment - and then two spirits are found in the world: one spirit of judgment and one spirit of impurity.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:88: Rabbi Elazar said, I must say here a teaching I learned from my father: come and see, thus we learn from the affliction of a house - that when an impure spirit dwells in a house, and the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to purify it, He sends the affliction of tzara'at into the house, so that the two contend with each other, and that affliction does not depart from the house, even though the impure spirit has departed from that house, until they demolish the house - stones and wood and everything - then the place is purified. In this same manner, one who has become impure and aroused an impure spirit that rests upon him - when the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to purify the world, He arouses a powerful spirit of judgment, found in the world, resting upon that impure spirit, and they contend with each other until it is removed from the world - and that powerful spirit of judgment does not depart from its place until it demolishes the place: limbs and bones and everything - then the world is purified and impure spirits are removed from it, and the world is found in purity. And therefore we have learned, he comes to become impure, they surely make him impure - woe to himself when an impure spirit rests upon him and is found in him in the world, for certainly we should know that the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to eliminate him from the world. Happy are the righteous, all of whom are holy, and are found in holiness before the Holy King, and a holy spirit rests upon them in this world and in the World to Come - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:89: And from this teaching it also appears that a penitent must perform great mortification for the sin of nocturnal emission, until he purifies himself from the impurity, for keri leads to impurity, and judgment must rest upon him until he is purified, as explained in the teaching, unless it is repaired through repentance, in the manner explained in the Tikkunim, in the teaching we copied, which said, "and endure much suffering, to remove that serpent from there," and as my teacher, peace be upon him, explained, whose explanation we copied above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:90: Now, nocturnal emission comes from several causes, and we must explain them. The first of them is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in Parashat Kedoshim (page 84a) concerning "do not turn to the idols" (Leviticus 19:4), which is the matter of gazing at women, which leads to forbidden thought and impurity, and he transgresses (ibid.), "and molten gods you shall not make for yourselves" - for since his whole body heats itself with the spirit of impurity, he is found making himself a molten god, and the explanation of the word "for yourselves" is as though it said "you shall not make yourselves into molten gods," along the lines explained. And so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Tetzaveh, page 182b) concerning "you shall not make yourself a molten god" (Exodus 34:17), concerning the matter of anger - that it said anger differs from all other impurities - these are its words: but this differs from all, and the entire body becomes impure within and without, and the soul, and everything becomes impure. And it said shortly after, and therefore it is written, "you shall not make yourself a molten god" - "for yourself," in order to bring harm upon yourself.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:91: And along these lines it said in the Zohar (Parashat Kedoshim, there), and whoever gazes at a woman's beauty by day comes to forbidden thoughts at night, and if that evil thought comes upon him he transgresses "you shall not make yourselves molten gods" - to this point. And the meaning of "if that evil thought comes upon him" is that the thought is drawn upon him until, through this, he comes to impurity - he is like one who worships idols, as explained at the beginning of the chapter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:92: Also, one must be careful not to engage in much conversation with any woman, especially with his wife when she is a menstruant - and along these lines they said in the first chapter of Avot (mishnah 5), "and do not engage in much conversation with a woman" - they said this of his own wife, all the more so of another's wife; from here the Sages said, whenever a person engages in much conversation with a woman, he causes evil to himself. And the matter of "causes evil to himself" is that he draws Lilith, who is called "evil," and she defiles him with a nocturnal emission. And so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayishlach, page 169b), on the verse (Psalms 91:10), "no evil shall befall you, nor shall a plague come near your tent" - for when a person walks a straight path and conducts himself in holiness, "evil," who is Lilith, and "plague," which are afflictions upon people, do not come near him - but if, God forbid, he does not walk a straight path, they make him impure. And along these lines we explain "evil to himself" - that he draws upon himself the evil Lilith to cause him to sin - and therefore his end is to descend to Gehinnom, to digest that evil that has attached to him. And he is idle from words of Torah - before the [rabbinic] immersion requirements for one with a nocturnal emission were abolished, such a person was forbidden [from] words of Torah, as in Ezra's enactment - and even today some are strict not to occupy themselves with Torah while impure.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:93: And speech with one's wife while a menstruant is explained in the Midrash Bamidbar Rabbah, Parashat Nazir (10:8) - these are its words: why did the Torah forbid the sediment of grapes, from which one does not become drunk, and also forbid eating everything that comes from the vine, things from which one does not become drunk? Why is this? From here we learn that a person is obligated to distance himself from what is ugly and from what resembles what is ugly - from here we learn that Torah made a fence for its own words. There we have learned (Avot, chapter 1, mishnah 1), "be deliberate in judgment, raise up many students, and make a fence for the Torah" - how does one make a fence for one's own words? In the manner Torah made a fence for its own words. Behold, it says (Leviticus 18:19), "and you shall not approach a woman in the impurity of her menstruation" - one might think, he may embrace her and kiss her and speak idle words with her - therefore Scripture says, "you shall not approach." She may sleep with him in her clothes - therefore Scripture says, "you shall not approach." One might think she may wash her face and paint her eyes and he may take the cup from her - therefore Scripture says (ibid. 15:33), "and she who is unwell in her menstruation" - all the days she is unwell she shall be in a state of ostracism. From here they said, whoever makes herself repulsive in the days of her menstruation, the spirit of the Sages is pleased with her; and whoever adorns herself in the days of her menstruation, the spirit of the Sages is not pleased with her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:94: Behold, it says (ibid. 18:6), "no man among you shall approach any close relative" - from here they said, a person should not seclude himself with women in one inn, even with his sister, and even with his daughter or his mother-in-law, because of what people might claim - here it says "shall not approach," and further it says "shall not approach": to a matter that leads to a transgression, "you shall not approach" - distance yourself from what is ugly and from what resembles what is ugly, for so the Sages said, distance yourself from a light sin lest it lead you to a severe one; run to a light mitzvah so that it lead you to a severe one - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:95: And concerning what is called "too much conversation with a woman," they were strict in Tractate Eruvin - these are their words: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili was walking on the road and encountered Beruriah. He said to her, by which way shall we go to Lod? She said to him, foolish Galilean, did the Sages not say, do not engage in much conversation with a woman? You should have said, "which way to Lod?" - to this point. And from here one who fears Heaven shall learn to minimize speech with a woman as much as possible, and especially with his wife when a menstruant, as explained in the teaching. And I found it written, "I was mute [ne'elamti], silent [dumiyah], I was still [hecheshayti]" (Psalms 39:3) - the acrostic is NIDAH [menstruant], to teach that one must especially minimize speech with her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:96: And just as one must be careful not to engage in much conversation, so one must be careful not to touch her, and the other detailed laws that Rabbeinu Yosef wrote in the Tur, Yoreh De'ah, and likewise not to gaze at her - for in transgressing any one of these, he draws upon himself the power of impurity that is in his wife, and possibly they shall defile him. And a warning about this we learn from Rashbi, peace be upon him (Zohar, Parashat Bereishit, page 20) - these are its words: in this manner, one whose wife is in her days of impurity, and guards her properly - all those days the supernal union is found with him and male and female are found - to this point. And from the affirmative you infer the negative: that if he does not guard her properly, the Shechinah departs from him. And you already know that the externals are called "these," being ready to rest immediately upon a person, as explained in Parashat Vayechi (Zohar, page 228a) - and possibly they shall defile him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:97: And especially in a place where holiness had been, and the holiness departed - there they run to attach themselves, and the proof is at a person's death, as explained in the Zohar (there, Parashat Vayechi, page 220a), that because holiness had rested there, they wish to attach themselves there. And for this reason my teacher, peace be upon him, would say that any person who conducts himself with abstinence and purity, and afterward departs from that holiness, may possibly be defiled, for the reason stated, that they pursue a place where holiness had been. And I add a further point: the husks are called vanity and emptiness, and they pursue only something that is empty like themselves - and since they find a vessel emptied of holiness, they attach to it, and especially according to what is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Mishpatim, end, page 111), that all their longing is after the thigh, and all the more so the thigh of Torah scholars - and therefore Torah scholars need extra warning, for these run to attach to them, and whatever side they find to attach to, they immediately attach and defile them. And of this it is said (Psalms 89:31-33), "if his children forsake My Torah and do not walk in My judgments, if they profane My statutes and do not keep My commandments, then I will visit their transgression with the rod and their iniquity with plagues [nega'im]" - and "plagues" are the afflictions of people that come from nocturnal emissions - and behold, it is explicit that when holiness departs, he is immediately visited with these sufferings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:98: And the reason the visitation for emitting seed in vain comes through the covenant is that the supernal covenant includes Torah and mitzvot in the secret of "all [kol] in heaven and earth" (I Chronicles 29:11), which we translate as, "that holds fast in heaven and earth" - it follows that in blemishing Torah, by not occupying himself with it properly, or in the mitzvot, he has profaned the supernal holy covenant, and therefore he is visited with the impurity of his own covenant.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:99: And this matter is hinted at in the Zohar (Parashat Vayishlach, end, page 176) - these are its words: concerning "more than all the merchant's powders" (Song of Songs 3:6) - another explanation: this is Joseph the righteous, and so on. Another explanation: why "merchant"? Rather, just as a shopkeeper has all the bundles, the boxes, and the powders of the perfumers in his hand, so too Joseph is the endurance of Torah, because he fulfilled it, since all the commandments of Torah are bound up with the guarding of the holy covenant - to this point. And so it says in the Zohar (Parashat Miketz, beginning of page 197): and therefore Joseph, who guarded the covenant, merited the supernal kingship and the lower kingship - and therefore whoever guards the holy covenant is as though he fulfilled the entire holy Torah, for the covenant is equal to the whole Torah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:100: And it is necessary to say the reason explained, that it is the secret of "all [kol] in all [kol]" - for otherwise, if a person guarded the covenant but did not recite the Shema and did not put on tefillin, and so on, would it be considered as though he had fulfilled all the mitzvot? Certainly not - rather, certainly it is as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:101: Also, the cause of nocturnal emission, in its essence and root, is because of the sin of the covenant of the tongue, as explained above (chapter 11), concerning (Psalms 34:14), "guard your tongue from evil." Also, one who reveals [secrets] to one unworthy is punished with nocturnal emission - and the reason is that the receptacle for the supernal secrets bestowed from Tzaddik, called Yud, is "the secret [sod] of the LORD is for those who fear Him," who are in the Shechinah, and this is the secret of "Hei for those who fear Him" - and when he is unworthy, he has drawn the light of Torah from within but found no vessel in which it can rest, and it goes out in vain to the externals - and it is found that he threshes within and scatters without, and this is the sin of Er and Onan - and therefore, measure for measure, his seed shall be spilled in vain and they shall defile him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:102: Also, one who recites blessings in vain is like one who emits seed in vain, and possibly they shall defile him - and one must be careful about this, especially the prayer leader, that he not repeat the Amidah if there are not surely nine to answer amen.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:103: Also, a cause of nocturnal emission is the cause of indulging in pleasure by sleeping the whole night, as explained above in chapter 5, and this is included in "if his children forsake My Torah." And the reason for this is that since he grows lax from the occupation with Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, becomes his enemy, as it is written (Proverbs 24:10), "if you are lax in the day of adversity, your strength is small" - and it is measure for measure: he did not wish to attach himself to the wife who fears the LORD, through the occupation with Torah, so he shall attach himself to the externality of the strange woman, and beget a demon to accuse him, and "eat of the fruit of his own deeds" - for no evil descends from above, but rather, once a person attaches himself to the Other Side, holiness departs from him, and then the externals, who are ready, rule over him, and he is called ELEH [these], as it is said (Deuteronomy 31:17), "because my God is not among me, these [eleh] evils have found me." And therefore, upon waking from sleep, he should hasten to rise - for if he does not rise and returns to sleep, he may sleep on his back, face upward, which is cursed by the mouth of the Sages, as we say (Berachot 13b), Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi cursed one who sleeps on his back.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:104: Also, the cause of nocturnal emission is explained in the Torah, in what is said (Leviticus 26:21), "and if you walk with Me keri [with hostile chance], and are not willing to listen to Me," and so on, and it is written (ibid. 26:28), "and I will walk with you in the wrath of keri," and so on - and Rashi, peace be upon him, explained: our Rabbis said, "irregular, occasional," happening only occasionally - so you shall walk irregularly in My commandments. And Menachem explained it as a term of withholding, and so (Proverbs 25:17), "let your foot be rare [hokar] in your neighbor's house," and so (ibid. 17:27), "a precious [yekar] spirit is a man of understanding" - and this word is close to the Targum of Onkelos, "kashyu," hardness, that they harden their hearts to refrain from drawing near to Me - to this point; and both explanations come to one intent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:105: And behold, what is written after it? "And I too will walk with you in the wrath of keri" - and Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Terumah, page 130a) - these are its words: "in the wrath of keri" - in that wrath that comes forth from the doorway of keri, and these are those [demons] that wander about at night; and at the time souls go out to ascend to be seen above, these go out and accuse them so that they cannot ascend, except for those holy pious ones, supernal ones, who split through the firmaments and the airs and ascend. And these bands of destroying angels go out and inform people of false things, and appear to them in various forms and laugh with them, until they spill seed - and they are called "the masters of keri," because those who come forth from the doorway of keri cause it to them - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:106: Therefore it is fitting for a person to be steady in divine service and faithful in it, like a pillar that does not sway from it - and so the word "brit" [covenant] means "endurance," along the lines of (Genesis 31:44), "come, let us make a covenant, I and you." And therefore whoever wishes to merit the attribute of Tzaddik must be faithful and strong in service - and of this it is said (Ecclesiastes 8:5), "whoever keeps a commandment shall know no evil thing." And you already know what was explained above concerning "evil."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:107: And so, if he breaches any of the fences of our Rabbis, they may possibly defile him - for the fences our Rabbis, of blessed memory, set up are so as not to give room for the external force to enter within to the holy place; and if he breaches a fence, a serpent shall bite him, since through the breach he made, he has given it room to enter. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 18b), that the sea is Torah, and "sand for the sea" means that it is like a chain for a dog, and one who loosens the chain causes the dog to bite him - and this alludes to the fences our Rabbis, of blessed memory, established - these are its words there: "and the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath" (Exodus 31:16) - this is the only daughter, who is a guard for Israel every single Sabbath, and whoever profanes her is not guarded by the Holy One, blessed be He, and moreover, it is said of her, "whoever profanes it shall surely be put to death" - whoever brings into her domain a maidservant, a profaned woman, a harlot - for her domain is the Sabbath boundary [techum], like the boundary and limit of the sea, of which it is said (Jeremiah 5:22), "I have placed sand as the boundary of the sea" - and what is this? (Hosea 2:1), "and the number of the children of Israel shall be like the sand of the sea" - and there is no "sea" except Torah - whoever transgresses it is as though he returns the world to chaos and void, and the Sabbath is equal to the whole Torah - whoever transgresses it is as though he returns the world to chaos and void - and therefore the verse [in Genesis] is juxtaposed to it (Genesis 1:2), "and the earth was chaos and void" - for it is [like] "sand for the sea," like the link of a chain for a dog: whoever removes it from its chain causes many bites of suffering to bite him. And concerning this David said (Psalms 22:21), "deliver my soul from the sword, my only one from the power of the dog" - and this is Samael, who is held by a collar and chain; on the Sabbath he is held by the collar - to this point. Behold, it is explicit that the Sabbath boundary and the sand for the sea are both one matter, to distance Samael and keep him away from holiness - and one who breaches the fence causes Samael to bite him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:108: And so, among the things one must be careful of, lest they defile him, is if he makes a vow - that he fulfill his vows to the service of the Name, as it is said (Psalms 15:4), "he swears to his own harm and does not retract" - and if he does not fulfill the mitzvah and breaks his vow, he may possibly become defiled, as it is written (Ecclesiastes 5:5), "do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin." And it is explained in the Midrash that this verse concerns vows, as we have copied their words above in chapter 14 - see there. And along these lines, "and destroy the work of your hands" is the covenant, as explained in Parashat Bereishit, page 8a, and we copied its words in chapter 11.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:109: And the reason is that the verse said (Numbers 30:3), "according to all that goes out of his mouth he shall do" - and the reason is, as we have already explained, that speech is spiritual, resembling physical seed - and just as, from the lower covenant, one must not emit seed in vain except into the female, so one must not emit speech in vain except to bring it to the place of action, which is the female - and thus the voice that goes forth unifies the covenant of the tongue with the female; and if, God forbid, he does not fulfill it, he has emitted seed in vain, which is the voice and speech that go forth from the covenant of the tongue - and therefore he shall also blemish the covenant of the member with seed in vain, for one transgression drags another.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:110: The remedy for the sin of nocturnal emission: first, he must immerse in a mikveh of forty se'ah, in order to purify himself from the impurity of the accursed external force - and even one who is lenient about immersion for the sake of marital union should not be lenient about this. And so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Bereishit, page 55a): and because one with a nocturnal emission comes from the side of the impure spirit, he must wash himself and purify himself from it, and the colleagues have already established this - to this point. And before this it speaks of the matter of Na'amah, the mother of the demons who ambush and are ready [for] all those who make people into those with nocturnal emissions.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:111: And if forty se'ah is not possible, he should strive to pour upon himself nine kabin. And if even this is not possible for him, he should at least wash the soiled place - and in Sefer Chasidim (siman 157) it is written that he should not think of words of Torah until he has rubbed his thighs with water - so it is fitting to do for the honor of Torah and prayer.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:112: And in the section on tzara'at, in the section on the zav [one with a discharge], they brought in the Yalkut, Tanna DeVei Eliyahu - these are its words: a person saw a nocturnal emission, which requires immersion; he said, who sees me? There is nothing to it - he set it aside from before him. Again he saw a nocturnal emission and said, who sees me? And so on, three times - he transgressed what is written (Job 33:29), "twice, three times, with a man" - for he becomes a zav from the very beginning of his ways, as it is said (Leviticus 15:2), "a man, a man who has a discharge" - what does it teach by "a man, a man"? To include a nocturnal occurrence. If he repents, he can be healed; if not, he remains in his presumed status until the day of his death, as it is said (ibid. 15:3), "and this shall be his impurity in his discharge" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:113: And concerning the merits of immersion, we have already written above in its place (Gate of Love, chapter 11), and we said that its special property is to return the soul to its place, for one who is impure has no soul [i.e., diminished spiritual vitality], and one who blemishes the covenant, his soul departs from him - and so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Lech Lecha, page 94a) - these are its words: for we have learned, at every time a person is marked with this holy sign of this letter, from it the Holy One, blessed be He, truly beholds him, and a holy soul attaches to him; if he does not merit, that he does not guard this sign, what is written? (Job 4:9), "by the breath of God they perish" - for the mark of the Holy One, blessed be He, was not guarded; and if he merits to guard it, the Shechinah does not separate from him - when is it established in him? When he is married and this sign enters into its place - to this point. And see further there to understand the matter properly, and to avoid lengthiness we have not copied all its words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:114: And incidentally we learn from this teaching a repair for the sign of the covenant, which is that he should strive to marry in his youth, in order to purify himself - and for this reason they said in Kiddushin (29b), Rav Chisda said, this is why I am superior to my colleagues, that I married at sixteen, and had I married at fourteen I would have said to Satan, an arrow in your eye - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:115: And in the Tikkunim (page 82b) it says: further, "a fruit tree" (Genesis 1:11) - this is the middle pillar, "making fruit" - this is Tzaddik, "whose seed is in it, upon the earth" - this is the Shechinah, in whom all seeds are included. And here is the mitzvah of being fruitful and multiplying, to make fruits and seeds - of which it is said (Isaiah 45:18), "He did not create it a chaos; He formed it to be inhabited" - and whoever refrains from being fruitful and multiplying is as though he returns this land to being a wasteland, and withholds blessings from it, each according to his own level - whoever blemishes below blemishes above, in the place his soul was hewn from - to this point. And if he has blemished, and cannot repair himself at the proper time, should God grant him a son, he should strive to marry him off before he comes to sin. And in this generation a person must distance his son and guard him from everything that might lead to a forbidden thought, before he marries.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:116: Further, the repair for the sign of the covenant is also through the occupation with Torah, as explained above in the teaching we copied from the Tikkunim (page 66b), and they explained in the Tikkunim (page 98b) that whoever has blemished the soul, his repair is through the occupation with Torah in the six orders of Mishnah - these are its words: and moreover, whoever brings his seed into a menstruant, maidservant, Gentile woman, or harlot, is as though he mixes together what the Holy One, blessed be He, separated, as it is written (Genesis 1:6), "and let it divide between water and water" - which are the waters of a menstruant and the waters of purity, that this is forbidden and that permitted, this fit and that unfit, this impure and that pure - these are the six orders in which the Mishnah was given, to distinguish between good and evil, which Adam and the generations that followed him mixed together - to this point. Further, see Tikkun 46.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:117: And if he strives to know the six orders of the Mishnah by heart, how good and how pleasant is his portion - for the essence of the Mishnah is to know it by heart, as it is said (Exodus 34:27), "for by these words I have made a covenant with you" - and the Oral Torah you are not permitted to write down (see Gittin 60b), and it was written only because of "it is time to act for the LORD" (Psalms 119:126) - and happy is he who knows it by heart, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Second Chamber (Zohar, Parashat Bereishit, page 42a). It said there that in the chamber called "the bone of the heavens" are seraphim with six wings, and it said afterward, these are they who burn those who do not care for the honor of their Master, and the secret of using the crown to one's own advantage; whoever reads and repeats the six orders of the Mishnah is one who knows how to arrange and bind the unification of his Master properly - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:118: And the essential knowledge of the Mishnah is that he strive to know it together with its explanation, and whoever reads it with its explanation shall not quickly forget it - and so it says in the Yerushalmi (Berachot, chapter 5, halachah 1): Rabbi Tanchum said, whoever understands his own learning does not quickly forget it. And along these lines, knowledge of Torah by heart is in the attribute of the male, for all remembering is in the male - and since this sin blemishes the sign of the covenant, which is in the place of the male, and descends to the place of forgetting, it is fitting that it be repaired through remembering, by knowing Torah by heart.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:119: And so, Torah is a repair so that one not come to nocturnal emission, and this matter is hinted at in the Zohar (Parashat Vayeshev, page 190a) - these are its words: Rabbi Elazar said, when that evil side comes to entice a person, he should draw himself toward Torah, and it [the evil side] shall separate from him. Come and see, for we have learned that when this evil side stands before the Holy One, blessed be He, to lead the world astray because of evil deeds, the Holy One, blessed be He, has compassion on the world and gives people counsel to be saved from it, so that it not have power over them or over their deeds. And what is this counsel? To occupy oneself with Torah and be saved from it. From where do we know this? As it is written (Proverbs 6:23), "for the commandment is a lamp and Torah is light, and the way of life is the reproofs of discipline" - what is written after it? "to guard you from the strange woman, from the smooth tongue of the foreign woman" - and this is the impure side, the Other Side, which stands always before the Holy One, blessed be He, to lead people astray in their sins - to this point, relevant here. Now, it is known that all the powers of nocturnal emission come from the "strange woman," and so it is explained in the Zohar: it is written, "for the commandment is a lamp and Torah is light," and so on, "to guard you" - it follows that Torah is a guard, to guard a person from these powers.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:120: And especially one who is unmarried should never lie down in bed to sleep until he is satisfied with Torah, as we say in Berachot (14a): Rabbi Yochanan said, whoever satisfies himself with words of Torah and goes to sleep is not brought bad tidings, as it is said (Proverbs 19:23), "and satisfied, he shall lodge, not visited by evil" - to this point. And it is already known that "evil" refers to one who emits seed in vain, along the lines of (Deuteronomy 23:10), "and you shall guard yourself from every evil thing," which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Avodah Zarah 20b), that one should not have a forbidden thought by day, and so on. And therefore it is fitting not to lie down until he has read much Torah, in a manner that he becomes satisfied - for just as a person satisfies himself with food, he should satisfy himself with Torah until he tires so that he cannot study further, like a person satisfied from abundant eating who cannot eat more.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:121: And nevertheless, if he occupied himself with Torah during the day and is satisfied with it, there is no obligation for him to prolong, at the beginning of the night, his occupation with Torah in a manner that he cannot rise for the night watch - and the wise man has his eyes in his head, and manages his affairs with judgment: that he occupy himself with Torah by day until he is satisfied, and at the beginning of the night he shall also occupy himself with Torah so that the soul ascend through the breath of Torah, but not to satiety, so that he not fail to rise for the night watch, which is the essential occupation with Torah, as it is said (Lamentations 2:19), "arise, cry out in the night," and as explained above (chapter 7).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:122: Further, the repair for the sign of the covenant is to be careful in all the attributes by which a person is called righteous, which depend on the supernal attribute of Tzaddik. And one of them is that he strive to rise at midnight, or from midnight onward, to occupy himself with Torah, and strive to join night to day through Torah, corresponding to what he separated between them - for one who rises at midnight is called righteous, as explained in Parashat Emor (page 90a), which we copied above (chapter 7), and it explained there that "He gives prey to those who fear Him" (Psalms 111:5) is said of those occupied with Torah from midnight onward, and the reason is that they participate with the attribute of fear.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:123: And so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Miketz, page 194b) that the verse, "the LORD favors those who fear Him, those who wait for His kindness" (Psalms 147:11), is said of those who rise from midnight onward, joining night to day in order to receive the thread of kindness - these are its words: "those who wait for His kindness" - say, these are those who occupy themselves with Torah at night and participate with the Shechinah, and when morning comes, they wait for His kindness, and so on - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:124: And concerning the merit of one who joins night to day through the occupation with Torah, Scripture explained by saying (Psalms 33:18-19), "behold, the eye of the LORD is upon those who fear Him, upon those who wait for His kindness, to deliver their soul from death and to keep them alive in famine" - and "the eye of the LORD" is explained in the Idra (Parashat Naso, page 129b) to be "the open eye" of Arich [Anpin], and so on - see there. And certainly, whoever does this repairs the attribute of Tzaddik together with the Shechinah, so that a thread of kindness is drawn for him and for her, as explained in several places - and corresponding to what he separated from the Shechinah by drawing a drop outward - and the secret of the drop is white, drawn from the side of the right, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 41a) concerning "and the manna was like coriander seed" (Numbers 11:7) - corresponding to this, he joins night to day to receive the thread of kindness. And so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayigash, page 207b), on the verse (Psalms 88:2), "LORD, God of my salvation, I have cried out by day, in the night I am before You" - that one who rises at midnight and occupies himself with Torah stands at the level of "Tzaddik, life of the worlds," and then, by day, he merits the thread of kindness, and this is what it means by "God of my salvation," for the thread of kindness is salvation, as it says (Psalms 60:7), "save with Your right hand" - and we shall not copy its words, so as not to be lengthy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:125: Further, one must be careful not to unite with his wife except from Sabbath to Sabbath, on Rosh Chodesh, and on festivals, for there is no unification above through Tzaddik except at the times mentioned, as it is written (see Ezekiel 46:1), "the gate facing east shall be closed the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened" - and so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Noach, beginning of page 75b), of blessed memory, on this verse: this verse must be contemplated, for it is a secret in what is said, "it shall be closed the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened" - why shall it be closed all those six working days? Rather, these are the weekdays, on which this gate shall be closed, so that the profane not make use of the holy. "But on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened" - for then there is the use of the holy with the holy, and then the moon shines to join with the sun - to this point, relevant here.
